name: fast-neural-style
statusSub: capture blocked — no attributed lineage was published
blocker: Three capture attempts on one compute target produced no usable attributed DAG. Attempt 1 published an attributed session with ZERO jobs while its anonymous twin carried them. Attempts 2 and 3 had their hosts terminated mid-job by the platform — attempt 2 one second before its third step began, attempt 3 thirty-four seconds into a lineage export that takes fifty-one. The training pipeline itself succeeded on every attempt that was allowed to finish; the artifact is published and public. The blocker is in the recording layer, not the workload.
summary: Fast neural style transfer (Johnson et al., perceptual losses + instance normalisation): a small convolutional TransformerNet trained to apply one fixed artistic style in a single forward pass, supervised by a frozen VGG-16 supplying a content loss on relu2_2 and a Gram-matrix style loss across four layers. Selected as the cleanest candidate available — three declared dependencies, torch.save only, no OS-package edge, no copy or link anywhere in the subdirectory — to test whether a simple workload yields a simple record. It did not. The model trained correctly three times; no attributed lineage was ever published, so the row is held with no DAG hash.
difficulty: 6/10 — trivial to run, hard to record
truncationNote: 1 of upstream's default 2 epochs, over Imagenette-320 (9,469 images) rather than the README's COCO-2014-train (82,783). Not converged.

truncation.note: upstream's default is --epochs 2 (neural_style/neural_style.py:196), read from the parser default, not guessed. The dataset is truncated on a second, independent axis: upstream's README trains on COCO 2014 train (82,783 images / 13 GB, a manual browser download with no fetch script); this row substitutes Imagenette-320 (9,469 images / 342 MB, one public tarball). That substitution is a scale decision, not a semantic one — the objective is a VGG-16 perceptual loss plus a Gram-matrix style term and depends on no COCO annotation, category or photograph, only on a varied corpus of natural images.

rebuild.fullRunEstimateBasis: g4dn.xlarge on-demand us-east-2 at $0.526/hr. Fixed portion 1,200 s = $0.175: instance boot 174 s, setup 216 s (provenance-CLI install, wheel sha256 verification, environment gates), dataset fetch 51 s, stylize 9 s, label+publish+lineage 310 s, teardown 280 s, plus ~77 s of per-step startup inside the train stage — of which the VGG-16 ImageNet weight download is 4.37 s / 553,433,881 bytes, measured directly into a throwaway TORCH_HOME rather than assumed. Variable portion 503 s/epoch = $0.0735, from a measured 18.8 images/s (8,669 images in 461 s between the first log line and the model save) over 9,469 images. Untruncated = 1,200 + 2×503 = 2,206 s = 36m46s = $0.322. Fixed and variable were measured on different attempts — the fixed portion from the only attempt that ran a complete lifecycle through teardown — because the platform terminated the other hosts early. Not costed out: upstream's own COCO-2014 recipe would be ~4,404 s/epoch at the same throughput (~2.9 h, ~$1.29 for 2 epochs) plus an untimed 13 GB download.

experimentUrlNote: upstream examples/fast_neural_style ships no experiment-logging integration — grepped the whole subdirectory for wandb, mlflow, trackio, tensorboard, SummaryWriter, comet, neptune and report_to: zero hits. There is no flag to enable. The metrics bridge only intercepts a wandb import the workload actually performs, so against this workload it is a guaranteed no-op; it was removed from the workflow rather than left in, so the record does not imply a logging path that does not exist. Adding wandb.init() to neural_style.py would have produced a link and forfeited the zero-upstream-lines property that makes the row evidence.

certification.resultCaveat: Not certified, and not certifiable as it stands: no attributed DAG was ever published, so there is no hash for a cold rebuild to start from. This operator performed the capture only — certification is done by a different agent so that what is measured is whether a stranger can rebuild from published materials, not whether the author can. result stays null until a cold rebuild produces an actual finding; it is never transcribed from an exit code.
